configurations.//: The real app: your own sign-in, your own Convex data. Start this one unless a task specifically needs one of the modes below. The e2e mode swaps the database out for fixtures, which looks like the app but is not, so nothing in it can be trusted or used.
configurations.name: next-dev

configurations.//: Signs in via /api/e2e-auth?role=... with no secret required, so admin screens can be inspected visually. E2E_AUTH_ENABLED also swaps convex/react for src/e2e/convexReactMock.tsx, so data is fixture data: good for verifying layout, navigation and role-dependent rendering, not for verifying real query results.
configurations.name: next-dev-e2e-auth

configurations.//: The production build, served locally. Use this to test anything that behaves differently in production — the content security policy in particular, which withholds 'unsafe-eval' on live and grants it in dev. Run `npm run build` first.
configurations.name: next-prod
